title: University IP / patents layer: foundational crypto, PQC, AI, and biometrics research -> licensees + the quantum/surveillance threads
source: Public record: USPTO patents; academic papers; university tech-transfer/licensing records; NIST PQC provenance; corporate acquisitions (Google/DNNresearch 2013). Catalog layer (#205). Structural overlay; edges graded. Purpose: wire ACADEMIA to the crypto/PQC/QRL, AI, and biometrics/surveillance blocks via the IP it originated.

edges.notes: RSA public-key crypto (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman, 1977) - patent US4405829, assigned to MIT; the foundation of modern public-key encryption/signatures (fact).
MIT licensed RSA to RSA Data Security (Rivest et al.) - the commercialization that seeded the crypto industry (fact).
Shor's algorithm on a CRQC breaks RSA (and ECC) - the reason the whole PQC migration exists; wires the university-crypto origin to the quantum tracker (fact of threat).

Robert McEliece (Caltech/JPL) proposed the code-based McEliece cryptosystem (1978) - now, ~47 years unbroken, a leading post-quantum candidate (fact); ties academia to the McEliece cryptanalysis watch (quantum-pqc).
Code-based crypto is one of the main PQC families (Classic McEliece; HQC) - the conservative, non-lattice branch (fact).
NTRU lattice cryptosystem (Hoffstein, Pipher, Silverman @ Brown, 1996) - the first practical lattice-based public-key scheme + a direct ancestor of today's lattice PQC (fact).
NTRU's IP passed via NTRU Cryptosystems -> Security Innovation -> OnBoard Security -> Qualcomm (2019) - the university-lattice-crypto-to-chipmaker pipeline (fact).
NTRU was a NIST PQC round-3 finalist + conceptual precursor to ML-KEM/ML-DSA (fact).
Oded Regev (Tel Aviv/NYU) introduced Learning With Errors (LWE, 2005) - the hardness assumption underpinning the NIST lattice standards (fact).
LWE/Module-LWE is the mathematical basis of ML-KEM (Kyber) + ML-DSA (Dilithium) - the primary NIST PQC standards (fact).
ML-KEM = FIPS 203 (2024) - the flagship post-quantum key-encapsulation standard; wires academic lattice theory to the deployed standard (fact).
XMSS (eXtended Merkle Signature Scheme; Buchmann/Dahmen/Huelsing @ TU Darmstadt) - stateful hash-based signatures, the most conservative PQC signatures (RFC 8391) (fact).
The Quantum Resistant Ledger is built on XMSS hash-based signatures - the direct academia-to-blockchain PQC deployment (fact); ties to the ECDSA-failure/PQC thread.
Hash-based signatures (XMSS/LMS -> SLH-DSA/FIPS 205) are the hash-only-assumption branch of PQC (fact).
The 2012 AlexNet breakthrough (Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Hinton @ Toronto) ignited the deep-learning revolution - the research origin of the modern AI boom (fact).
Google acquired DNNresearch (Hinton's spinout) in 2013, bringing Hinton + the AlexNet team in-house - the academia-to-Big-Tech AI pipeline (Sutskever later co-founded OpenAI) (fact).
Stanford's ImageNet (Fei-Fei Li, 2009) provided the dataset/benchmark that AlexNet won - the fuel for the deep-learning takeoff (fact).
Eigenfaces (Turk & Pentland, MIT Media Lab, 1991) - the first practical automated face-recognition method - the academic root of facial recognition (fact).
Eigenfaces seeded the facial-recognition field that (with deep learning) became mass biometric surveillance (fact).
Deep-learning facial recognition underpins Clearview AI's scraped-face matching sold to police - the academic-method-to-surveillance-product endpoint (fact).
Face matching is a core modality of digital-ID/onboarding systems - wiring the biometrics IP to the Digital_ID thread (fact).
John Daugman (Cambridge) invented + patented the dominant iris-recognition algorithm (US5291560) - licensed via Iridian/L-1 into border/ID systems worldwide (fact).
Iris biometrics (the Daugman lineage) underpin Worldcoin's Orb-scanned 'World ID' - the newest privatized iris-ID deployment (fact of modality).
Iris is a high-assurance biometric used in national ID (India's Aadhaar) + border systems - wiring Cambridge IP to the Digital_ID thread (fact).
